Messages.Author: Akantes
Messages.Body:
Before I get into an argument with this.

I bleed my prey, and my prey tries to block. I play false resonance at
superior. My prey plays either Telepathic Misdirection or My Enemy's
Enemy to redirect the bleed to somewhere else.

If I burn the blood to cancel the aus-card which was bounce, is the
bleed resolved in the same matter as it would be, if the bounce would
have been cancelled with DI from some other player?

My guess is yes, but I'd want to be sure.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Canceling the card via False Resonance is handled just the same way it would be
if it were canceled by some other effect, yes.

Messages.Author: Salem
Messages.Body:


So basically they have to decline to block before they are allowed to
play their bounce card (either explicitly, or it's implied by them
trying to play the bounce card in the first place).
Then you cancel it.
So then they can't block, because they've already declined.

Nice!
